newsitem.title: CYPRUS: Court finds Cypriot man guilty in AIDS case.
newsitem.headline: Court finds Cypriot man guilty in AIDS case.

text.p: A Cyprus court on Tuesday found a Greek Cypriot fisherman guilty of recklessly transmitting the deadly virus that causes AIDS to his English lover, Janette Pink.

"From January 1994 and for a period of two years, the accused repeatedly came in sexual contact with Janette Pink without the use of a condom. In no case did he tell her he was a carrier of the disease," District Court Judge Antonis Liatsos told the accused, Pavlos Georgiou, aged 40.
Georgiou slouched over the dock as the judge read the verdict, which lasted 50 minutes. He is to be sentenced on Thursday.
Pink, 45, from Basildon, England, did not come to Cyprus for the verdict at the end of a three-month trial.
Georgiou, a father of four, is HIV positive but shows no visible signs of illness. He had denied Pink's accusation that he lied to her about having the disease.
His youngest son is HIV positive and his wife died in 1994 of an AIDS-related illness.
Pink tested HIV positive in October 1994, nine months after her affair with Georgiou started.
The charge carries a sentence of up to two years in jail, a 1,500 Cyprus pound ($2,770) fine, or both.
